summary: Two examples in AC-06.6.5 fail, and dev refinement raised two major questions about the 'incomplete - HR must complete' state. Technical wording also leaks into the spec (D-045). Several rules and items are only partly traced to cited sources. The calculator-coverage open question is non-blocking, but it needs sign-off before go-live.

findings.title: AC-06.6.5 examples fail: the 'incomplete' case has no passing test
findings.why: After an HR change, the tariff code is specified as 'incomplete - HR must complete' (D-053). The computed code instead returns a partial value (A0 / N). The first example expects Denomination 'required', which contradicts D-053. The second never shows the unasked spouse-employment question. The incomplete-state behaviour is therefore untested and ambiguous.
findings.evidence: examples: AC-06.6.5 (both cases pass=false); dev_refinement US-06.6 (major)
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml that the tariff code is 'incomplete - HR must complete' whenever a required input was never asked. Then fix both example tables: show the unasked question as 'not asked' and expect 'incomplete'. Fix the rule expression so it returns 'incomplete' rather than a partial code.

findings.title: Scope of the 'incomplete' state is undefined for pension fund results
findings.why: The spec covers only the tariff code and 'subject to source tax'. It does not say what the fund canton, or the fund civil status Married without a spouse date of birth, show after an HR change that makes an unasked answer applicable. Engineering would have to guess.
findings.action: Decide which derived results go 'incomplete' (for example canton and the spouse date of birth for the fund). Or decide that HR must enter the missing value, and state that in US-01.6.

findings.title: tariff_code rule contradicts its own statement
findings.why: The expression uses if_else(child_count,1,0), which yields only 0 or 1. The statement and the calculator facts require the number of counted children (for example C3Y). Codes for two or more children would be wrong.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.tariff_code; OQ-calculator-coverage (H3N/P3N, more than 3 children)
findings.action: Correct the expression to use the child count (or its capped value). Add examples for 2 and 3 children. Confirm the behaviour for more than 3 children with the domain expert.

findings.title: Technical wording leaks into the spec
findings.why: D-045 forbids internal-formula language in business text. ISO 3166 is implementation vocabulary, and 'free text is not accepted' dictates how the input behaves.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md and information.md ('internal expression'); US-02.3; item.address_country, nationality, spouse_nationality; AC-02.3.1, AC-05.1.2, AC-05.2.3
findings.action: Remove the 'internal expression' sentence. Say 'a list of countries (English names) plus stateless'. Drop the free-text prohibition and keep only 'the country is required'.

findings.title: Rules rely on facts and gating that no cited source backs
findings.why: Liechtenstein/non_return_days_45 gating, the tariff purposes, the 'cannot occur for onboarding' claim and several table rows are not backed by the cited facts. Some rows cite facts that are not in the rule's citation list. That weakens traceability and risks wrong rules.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: rule.questionnaire_flow, base_tariff_letter, cross_border_tariff, tariff_letter, calculator_residence, pension_fund_canton, liechtenstein_no_source_tax; items has_children, child_*, spouse_gainful_employment
findings.action: Add the missing citations (D-002, D-047, F-...3432a9, e22d17, f86c6b, 5af8d0). Where no source exists, mark the claim as inferred in decisions.yaml or remove it.

findings.title: Unconfirmed rule: at least one child block is required
findings.why: AC-07.2.1 requires at least one child block and every child question to be required. No source backs either. The behaviour when the last block is removed is undefined.
findings.action: Confirm with HR. Decide whether removing the last child block is blocked or sets 'has children' to no.

findings.title: Inconsistent expected values across example tables
findings.why: The same question is marked 'asked' in some stories and 'required' in others. '–' is used for inputs and for results with mismatched values, and Married/Single spouse date of birth differs from Divorced/Widowed. Testers cannot tell what to assert.
findings.action: Define a single vocabulary (required / optional / not asked) and what '–' means. Align the tables to it and fix the US-04.4 rows.

findings.title: Conflicting rules on when a missing answer blocks the employee
findings.why: Some stories block leaving the step and others block only submission. US-01.7 allows saving a partly filled step.
findings.action: Decide that missing answers block only submission, not navigation. Align the stories and say how an incomplete step is shown.

findings.title: Tariff calculator coverage is unverified (non-blocking)
findings.why: Unexplored paths (A/B/H residence block, inferred per-child rows, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N) could produce wrong source tax codes. Some calculator facts are only partly verified (Q16 residence meaning, Q14, Q19, Q to the cross-border tariff).
findings.evidence: open_questions OQ-calculator-coverage; fact_judge F-zh_source_tax_calculator-037b1c, 64ac33, dc0ae9, c8aa5e, 2754e8; inferred_items
findings.action: Schedule the domain expert comparison against the Zurich calculator before go-live. Confirm the meaning of Q14, Q16 and Q19.

findings.title: Certificate-of-residence and start-date semantics unclear (minor)
findings.why: 'Provided' versus 'has' a certificate changes what HR expects. The first-working-day check has no defined 'sent' date, and past dates are not addressed. The insurance start date validation (the 1st of a month) has no source for its error behaviour.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-08.2, US-03.1; coverage F-pension_portal-e45e5b unused
findings.action: Decide: 'yes' means already given to HR. Define the reference date for the one-year window and whether past dates are allowed. State the start-date error wording as a product decision.
